subject: Logic
title: Priors and Posteriors
description: A quick win: understand Priors and Posteriors.

hook.text: Before any data, you have a guess. After new evidence, your guess should shift. By how much?

buildup.text: The prior is your belief before seeing evidence. The posterior is your belief after updating with evidence.

discovery.text: Strong priors resist change—you need overwhelming evidence. Weak priors shift easily with even a little data.

twist.text: Choosing the right prior matters enormously. A biased prior can distort every conclusion that follows.

climax.text: Good Bayesian thinking means being honest about your starting beliefs—and willing to update them.

quiz.question: What is a 'prior' in Bayesian reasoning?
